payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce negative-electrolyte crossover, a principal aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. An independent audit corrected the prototype’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity knee, retracting the earlier 12,000-cycle claim because it used un-normalized depth of discharge. The cell’s confirmed gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh production scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
